modules.title: AI-Augmented Web, API & Mobile Application Security

modules.title: Adversarial AI & AI Red Teaming
modules.description: Covers jailbreaks, prompt injection, and model evasion as deliberate attack techniques against AI systems, treating AI red teaming as its own discipline.

ai-augmented-offensive-security.audience: [{"text":"Final-year students & recent graduates","icon":"GraduationCap"},{"text":"Working IT professionals upskilling into security","icon":"Briefcase"}]
ai-augmented-offensive-security.labs: OSINT Target Profile — Build a passive recon profile of a lab target using public records, DNS/WHOIS, and social footprint data before touching a single port. Active Enumeration Sweep — Run active scans to map live hosts, open services, and versions across a lab network. Exploit & Escalate — Exploit a vulnerable lab host and chain a privilege-escalation technique to full control. AI-Assisted Recon Script — Direct an AI copilot to build a Python recon script, then debug and extend it against a live target. OWASP Top 10 Lab Walkthrough — Break a deliberately vulnerable web app across multiple OWASP Top 10 categories and document each finding.

modules.title: State of AI in Cybersecurity
modules.description: Surveys the current offense, defense, and risk landscape around AI, giving learners a grounded overview of where AI is actually changing attacker and defender workflows today.

modules.title: LLM & Prompt-Injection Security Basics
modules.description: Covers how AI-powered applications get attacked, focusing on prompt injection as the foundational vulnerability class specific to LLM-based systems.

modules.title: Using AI Copilots for Triage & Recon
modules.description: Hands-on practice applying AI copilots to real triage and reconnaissance tasks, pulled directly from our SOC and offensive security modules.

modules.title: AI Governance Basics
modules.description: Introduces the NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act at a high level, closing with a mini project that applies the month's concepts to a small practical scenario.

esecurityin-ai-security-foundations.audience: [{"text":"Final-year students & recent graduates","icon":"GraduationCap"},{"text":"Working IT professionals upskilling into security","icon":"Briefcase"}]
esecurityin-ai-security-foundations.labs: Risk Assessment Walkthrough — Score a sample organization's assets and produce a basic risk register using CIA-triad thinking. Threat Landscape Mapping — Research a named threat-actor group and map its motivations onto a target industry profile. AI-Assisted Recon Script — Get hands-on with an AI copilot inside a real security workflow, not just theory. IOC Enrichment Exercise — Enrich a set of raw indicators of compromise and write a short campaign-attribution brief.

modules.title: Cybersecurity Foundations
modules.description: Establishes the analyst mindset before any tooling: the CIA triad, risk vs. threat vs. vulnerability, security control classification, and the Cyber Kill Chain mapped against MITRE ATT&CK. Learners close the module by building a one-page threat profile for a fictional organization — their first structured security deliverable.

modules.title: Networking Fundamentals
modules.description: Covers the OSI/TCP-IP model, protocol-level vulnerabilities, and firewall/VLAN segmentation through live packet capture. The centerpiece is watching an ARP poisoning attack unfold byte-by-byte in real traffic — the moment most learners cite as making networking attacks "click" for the first time.

modules.title: Linux Essentials for Cybersecurity
modules.description: Filesystem permissions, process management, CLI triage tools, and SSH hardening — taught entirely on a real Linux VM, not a simulator. Learners leave with a personalized host-hardening checklist and the experience of scoring a peer's hardened system against a professional rubric.

modules.title: Windows Security & PowerShell Fundamentals
modules.description: Active Directory structure, GPO security, Windows event log analysis, and PowerShell scripting for security automation. Learners use BloodHound to discover a hidden privilege-escalation path in a lab AD — the same technique behind the Colonial Pipeline breach — and then close it.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Security Programming & Automation
modules.description: Python for log parsing, regex-based IOC extraction, and API-driven recon (Shodan, VirusTotal), with AI used to accelerate — and critically validate — generated code. The module closes with learners publishing a working AI-augmented security tool to GitHub: a recruiter-visible artifact by Week 5.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Threat Intelligence
modules.description: Threat intel frameworks, the Diamond Model, malware behavior analysis in sandboxed environments, and structured IOC triage using MISP. Learners analyze a real APT campaign (e.g., Lazarus Group) with an AI co-analyst and produce the exact threat-profile format a Day-1 SOC analyst submits.

modules.title: Footprinting, Reconnaissance & Enumeration
modules.description: Passive and active OSINT techniques, Nmap scanning, and service/user enumeration. Learners first map their own digital footprint — exposed emails, credentials, linked accounts — making the risk of reconnaissance personally real before ever pointing a tool at a target network.

modules.title: Vulnerability Assessment, Exploitation & Privilege Escalation
modules.description: Methodology for identifying, assessing, and ethically exploiting software and system vulnerabilities: Nessus and OpenVAS vulnerability scanning, CVE prioritization, exploit modification, and Metasploit fundamentals. Covers Linux and Windows local privilege escalation — SUID abuse, kernel exploits, service misconfigurations, and token impersonation — with hands-on practice on vulnerable target machines.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Web, API & Mobile Application Security
modules.description: OWASP Web and API Top 10 testing with Burp Suite, mobile static analysis with MobSF, and evaluation of AI-agent/LLM-integrated endpoints for prompt-injection and auth-flow abuse. Learners run a bug-bounty-style assessment on a vulnerable e-commerce platform and its AI chatbot, producing a tri-layer report: executive summary, technical findings, and developer remediation guide.

modules.title: Network Penetration Testing & Wireless Security
modules.description: Internal network pentest methodology — initial access, lateral movement, pivoting — using Responder, CrackMapExec, and Impacket, plus WPA2/3 wireless assessment. The module ends with a full timed pentest engagement under exam-like conditions, producing a report in the exact format used by Big-4 consulting firms.

modules.title: Cloud & AWS Security Fundamentals
modules.description: The shared responsibility model, least-privilege IAM design, and native AWS security services (GuardDuty, CloudTrail, Security Hub). Learners intentionally misconfigure — then detect, alert on, and remediate — a live S3 data exposure in a real AWS account, running the full attacker-to-defender loop on genuine cloud infrastructure.

modules.title: AI-Augmented SOC Fundamentals
modules.description: SOC tiering, alert triage workflows, and incident case management using TheHive. The module's capstone is a 90-minute SOC shift simulation with an AI copilot — 20 real-world-modeled tickets under a live clock, the closest approximation to Day-1 SOC work most learners will encounter before their first job.

modules.title: AI-Augmented SIEM Engineering & Threat Detection
modules.description: Log ingestion and correlation rule building in Splunk, ATT&CK coverage mapping, and AI-assisted false-positive reduction. Learners author an original Sigma detection rule for a real ATT&CK technique and publish it to a shared cohort detection library — a public engineering artifact recruiters can verify.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Endpoint Security, XDR & Threat Hunting
modules.description: Endpoint telemetry investigation, IOC-driven and behaviour-based hunting with YARA and OSQuery, and AI/SOAR-assisted triage. Includes a live lab demonstrating a prompt-injection attack against a security automation workflow — rare, formal classroom coverage of an emerging AI-security risk.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Incident Response & Digital Forensics
modules.description: The full 6-phase IR lifecycle, disk and memory forensics with FTK Imager and Volatility 3, timeline reconstruction, and chain-of-custody documentation. Learners produce a court-admissible-format IR report on a simulated ransomware breach, drafted with an AI copilot and reviewed against real DFIR consulting-firm rubrics.

modules.title: Capstone: Red-vs-Blue Simulation + GRC + Portfolio
modules.description: The program's final assessment - not an exam, but a live engagement. Learners run a full offensive kill chain while an opposing Blue Team detects and responds in real time, with SIEM/XDR telemetry monitored live throughout. Findings are mapped to ISO 27001:2022 or NIST CSF controls, and the entire output is packaged into a resume-ready portfolio - executive writeup, technical appendix, and GitHub evidence - then presented to an external industry panel.

modules.title: Cybersecurity Foundations

Also introduces baseline GRC concepts so learners understand the frameworks shaping every security decision downstream. This module is the anchor point every other competency in the program builds on.

modules.title: Networking Fundamentals
modules.description: Covers the OSI and TCP/IP models, how packets actually move across a network, and how to read and interpret traffic using tools like Wireshark. Learners build the protocol-level fluency — DNS, DHCP, HTTP/S, routing basics — needed to understand how networks work and how they can be attacked or defended. Foundational for every downstream offensive or defensive module.

modules.title: Linux Essentials for Cybersecurity
modules.description: Builds real command-line fluency: navigating the filesystem, managing permissions and users, working with processes, and scripting basic automation in Bash. Learners also cover host-hardening basics since Linux underpins the majority of real-world servers and security tooling. Essential groundwork for SOC analysts and penetration testers alike.

modules.title: Windows Security & PowerShell Fundamentals
modules.description: Covers Active Directory structure, Group Policy Objects, and Windows event logging, alongside practical PowerShell scripting. Learners see how Windows environments are typically attacked and how the same telemetry is used defensively. Central to both attack-path work and detection engineering.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Security Programming & Automation
modules.description: Teaches practical Python scripting for security tasks — parsing logs, automating recon, building simple tooling — paired with AI copilots that accelerate that workflow. Learners practice prompting AI assistants effectively for code generation and automation. Builds the automation mindset expected of modern practitioners on both offense and defense.

modules.title: AI-Augmented Threat Intelligence
modules.description: Covers collecting, analyzing, and enriching indicators of compromise and campaign data, using AI tooling to accelerate correlation across large data sets. Learners practice translating raw intelligence into actionable outputs. Acts as the connective layer between findings, detection, and business-level risk communication.

modules.title: Cloud & AWS Security Fundamentals
modules.description: Covers AWS IAM configuration, common misconfiguration patterns, and cloud-native attack surfaces such as exposed storage and over-permissioned roles. Learners practice hunting for and remediating the misconfigurations most responsible for real-world cloud breaches. Essential for any role touching modern, cloud-hosted infrastructure.
